gloss: to applaud; to cheer; to acclaim

definitions.gloss: to applaud; to cheer; to acclaim; to give an ovation
definitions.explanation: To express enthusiastic approval or admiration for someone's achievement or performance, either literally through clapping or figuratively through praise.

examples.japanese: {観客|かんきゃく}が{喝采|かっさい}を{送|おく}った。
{選手|せんしゅ}たちに{惜|お}しみない{喝采|かっさい}を{送|おく}った。
examples.english: They gave the players wholehearted applause.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{勇気|ゆうき}ある{行動|こうどう}に、{世界中|せかいじゅう}から{喝采|かっさい}が{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: His courageous actions were applauded from around the world.

notes:
A set expression combining {喝采|かっさい} (cheers, applause) with {送|おく}る (to send). The expression carries a sense of warm, enthusiastic praise and is more literary than simple {拍手|はくしゅ}する. Often used in news writing and formal contexts to describe acclaim for achievements.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {惜|お}しみない{喝采|かっさい}を{送|おく}る: to give unstinting applause
- {大|おお}きな{喝采|かっさい}を{送|おく}る: to give great applause
- {喝采|かっさい}を{浴|あ}びる: to receive applause (from the recipient's perspective)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拍手|はくしゅ}を{送|おく}る: to send applause — more literal, focused on clapping
- {声援|せいえん}を{送|おく}る: to send cheers — focused on vocal support
- {称賛|しょうさん}する: to praise — a more general word for praising
